reasoning_summary: Selected features cover broad semantic groups relevant to credit risk including credit score, loan terms, income and capacity, exposure, revolving utilization, account opening activity, credit history length, mortgage history, recent inquiries, and delinquency behavior. Priority was given to features with zero missingness, stable and interpretable credit-risk meaning, and durable signals of repayment behavior and indebtedness. Redundancy was controlled by preferring representative aggregates over near-duplicates, especially within the same semantic group, and avoiding brittle or leakage-prone variables. Features with fixed business-rule bands or log/sqrt transformations were included only when they add interpretability or stability. Interactions with FICO or verification status were included when they add distinct information. This broad candidate set supports stable out-of-time generalization and downstream statistical selection.
